title: Mo Sees the Sky
markdown:
Deep down where the earth smells warm and cozy, lived a little mole named Mo. Mo loved his burrow, especially his bed of soft leaves that felt like a gentle hug. But Mo had a quiet wish, a wish that tickled him. Mo had never, ever seen the sky. He’d wiggle his little nose and wonder, “What is the sky like? Is it like a big, soft blanket? Or like sparkly stones all glowing softly?” But it stayed a mystery, hidden from his sleepy mole eyes.

One soft evening, as Mo peeked just a tiny bit out of his burrow, he saw a gentle glow, pulsing like a sleepy heart. It was Starla, the glowworm, her tiny light twinkling like a friendly star that had come to visit. Starla had a bright glow and an even brighter smile, always ready with a kind word. “Oh, hello, Mo,” she whispered, her voice like the rustle of leaves in a soft breeze. “Are you dreaming of the world above today?”

Mo blinked his small eyes, used to the gentle dark of his home. “Oh, Starla, yes!” he sighed, his voice a soft rumble. “I wonder and wonder, but I don’t know what it looks like. It all stays hidden.” A tiny worry fluttered in his tummy, like a little pebble in his soft paw. *This is worry,* he realized, and it made him want to snuggle deeper into his cozy burrow. He knew that soon, the last glimmer of daylight would be gone, and if he didn't go now, he’d have to wait for another night.

Starla tilted her head, her glow dimming a little, as if she were thinking very hard. “Well, Mo,” she said softly, her voice like a sleepy dove’s coo, “I can show you. There’s a gentle hill not too far away, where the grass grows tall and soft. If we go to the very top, where the air is so still, you can see the sky. It’s a peaceful place.”

Mo wiggled his whiskers, his little heart thumping a soft beat. Going up, up, up felt a little new. He was used to the comforting ground beneath his paws. But Starla’s light was so warm, a little beacon of safety, and her voice was as kind as a lullaby. “Really?” he asked, his voice a soft whisper, full of hopeful surprise. “You’ll show me?”

“Of course, little Mo,” Starla chirped, her light pulsing with a happy glow. “We’ll go slowly. I’ll be right here with you. Just follow my light.”

And so, Mo took a deep breath that smelled of sweet dew, and set out to follow Starla. The hill wasn't steep at all; it was like a gentle swell, a smooth curve rising towards the soft evening. Mo felt his paws sink a little into the cool grass. Sometimes, his heart would beat a little faster, and he’d look back towards his burrow, his safe, warm home. But then he’d see Starla’s steady glow ahead, like a tiny moon leading him on. "Are you alright, Mo?" Starla would ask, her light pulsing gently.

“Yes, Starla,” Mo would reply, his voice still a little soft, but he kept walking, one paw in front of the other. He knew Starla would keep him safe.

Slowly, ever so slowly, they reached the very top of the hill. The air here was soft and still, smelling of sweet flowers. Mo took a big, deep breath, and then, with a little gulp, he looked up. Oh, my dears, what a wonderful sight met his eyes. The sky was a deep, dark blue, like the deepest blue crayon, stretching out so far it seemed to go on forever, like the softest silk. And all over the sky, like little shiny bits of glitter, were stars. Millions and millions of them, some shining bright, others shyly twinkling.

Mo’s little mole heart felt a big, happy feeling of amazement. He looked at Starla, whose gentle light added to the twinkling magic. “Oh, Starla,” he whispered, his voice filled with awe, “it’s… it’s beautiful. More beautiful than I ever imagined.”

Starla nestled close to Mo’s soft fur, her glow warming his cheek. “Yes, little Mo,” she agreed, her voice a soft hum. “It is. And see? The night is full of lovely light, if you only look with a happy heart.”

They sat there for a long time, watching the stars drift by. The air was cool and still, and the only sounds were the soft chirping of sleepy crickets and the gentle whisper of the breeze singing a quiet lullaby. Mo felt so peaceful, so safe, snuggled next to his kind friend, bathed in the soft light of the stars and Starla’s own glow. His eyes began to feel heavy, like little curtains wanting to close, and a big, warm yawn stretched his little mole mouth wide. "I feel so sleepy," he murmured, his voice already soft and lulling.

Starla gave him a warm little nudge. “Then it’s time to rest, little Mo,” she said kindly. “You’ve seen the sky, and it was a wonderful adventure. Now, it’s time for sweet dreams.”

Together, they ambled back down the gentle hill, Starla’s light a guiding star all the way to Mo’s burrow. Mo snuggled into his leafy bed, his nose twitching happily, already feeling the pull of sleep. He closed his eyes, and in his dreams, he saw the vast, dark blue sky, sprinkled with a million twinkling stars, all shining down on him with gentle, peaceful light, like a warm hug. And he knew, with a happy little sigh, that he would dream of the stars every night.
characters: Mo the mole, Starla the glowworm
